stage: exploratory CPU screening on existing frozen features
question: Does penalizing class-conditional source-user drift improve full three-view classification beyond an ordinary linear fusion readout?
input: SHA-verified multiview_s2026/foldH/predictions.npz features [9300,3,256] from each fold's frozen source-trained encoder
split: test H, validation H%8+1, other six users train; no target labels in fitting
scaling: feature mean and standard deviation from training examples only
training_weight: equal classes, then equal available users within each class, then equal examples within each user-class cell
objective: sum_i w_i ||x_i W + b - onehot(y_i)||^2 + alpha ||W||^2 + eta mean_uc ||(mean_x_uc - mean_u(mean_x_uc)) W||^2
selection: maximum validation macro accuracy; ties retain the earliest grid entry; independent selection for ridge and penalized ridge
test: one final prediction per selected model; report all eight users, mean and worst user macro accuracy, and paired differences
continue_criterion: penalized ridge exceeds both original LTR and plain ridge by at least 1 percentage point in mean user macro accuracy and improves plain ridge for at least 6 of 8 users
limits: No encoder retraining, no independent-user confirmation, no novelty claim, no end-to-end deployment claim because old checkpoints were not transferred. This tests a mechanism before spending on new network training.
